meta.title: RDK Course | Lesson 10: RDK S100 Hardware Codec Loop

slides.title: RDK S100 [gradient]Codec Loop[/gradient]
slides.lead: Use two C++ programs to connect Camera, hardware encoding, RTSP, hardware decoding, VPS, and HDMI display

cards.title: RDK S100
cards.body: RDK S100 with a supported RDK OS; BSP provides Camera, VPU, and HDMI drivers

cards.title: Camera Input
cards.body: IMX219 example captures 1920×1080@30fps NV12

cards.title: H.264 Transport
cards.body: Hardware encoder targets 8000 kbit/s over local RTSP/TCP

cards.title: Visible Result
cards.body: VPS scales to 800×480; Display channel 11 outputs through HDMI

slides.data_title: What You Will Be Able to Do
slides.title: What You Will Be Able to Do
slides.lead: Run the demo and explain the format and responsibility at every stage
items: Place Bayer RAW, NV12, H.264, RTP, and RTSP in the pipeline
Explain why encoding reduces bandwidth and decoding restores images
Open Camera and create a hardware encoder with libspcdev
Use GStreamer for RTP packetization, RTSP sessions, and depacketization
Use hardware Decoder, VPS, and Display for live HDMI output
Locate faults in Camera, Codec, RTSP, VPS, or Display from logs

cards.title: Board and OS
cards.body: RDK S100 with a supported RDK OS and working BSP codec drivers

cards.title: MIPI Camera
cards.body: Use a BSP-supported sensor and Camera expansion board; power off before adjusting cables

cards.title: HDMI Display
cards.body: Must support 800×480; power and select HDMI before booting S100

cards.title: Two Terminals
cards.body: Run Server and Client separately so each log remains visible

slides.title: Run Four Preflight Checks
slides.lead: Verify the board, drivers, display mode, and development interface before building

cards.title: ① Model and Drivers
cards.note: The model should contain RDK S100 and codec device nodes should exist

cards.title: ② HDMI Mode
cards.note: The HDMI connector must be connected and its mode list must include 800x480

cards.title: ③ BSP Interface
cards.note: Confirm that the BSP provides the header and libspcdev

cards.title: ④ GStreamer
cards.code: gst-inspect-1.0 appsrc && gst-inspect-1.0 rtspsrc && gst-inspect-1.0 rtph264pay
cards.note: Also check appsink, h264parse, and rtph264depay

slides.title: Build Directly on the Board
slides.lead: Configure and link on the S100 itself; do not copy binaries or libraries from another architecture

cards.title: ① Install Dependencies
cards.code: sudo apt install -y build-essential cmake pkg-config libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev libgstrtspserver-1.0-dev
cards.note: Install the compiler, GStreamer, and RTSP Server development packages

cards.title: ③ Build
cards.note: This small project builds reliably with -j2

cards.title: ④ Verify Outputs
cards.note: Both Server and Client executables should be present

cards.title: Raw Video Is Large
cards.body: One 1080p NV12 frame is 3,110,400 bytes; 30fps is about 746.5 Mbit/s

cards.title: Encoding Cuts Bandwidth
cards.body: Hardware encoding targets about 8 Mbit/s and emits SPS, PPS, and IDR

cards.title: Decoding Restores Images
cards.body: Compressed data cannot enter VPS; depay RTP, then decode to NV12

cards.title: Camera / VIO
cards.body: sp_open_camera_v2 opens Camera, ISP, and NV12 output

cards.title: Encoder
cards.body: sp_start_encode creates the H.264 hardware encoder

cards.title: GStreamer
cards.body: Handles RTP, RTSP, reception, and depay—not image decoding

cards.title: Decoder
cards.body: sp_decoder_set_image submits H.264 access units to VDEC

cards.title: VPS
cards.body: sp_open_vps scales 1920×1080 NV12 to 800×480

cards.title: Display
cards.body: sp_start_display outputs HDMI through S100 channel 11

slides.title: Keep These Parameters Separate
slides.lead: Codec dimensions stay consistent end to end; VPS adapts the image to the display

cards.title: Sensor Size
cards.body: Server --sensor-width/--sensor-height: Camera RAW input

cards.title: Codec Size
cards.body: Both --width/--height pairs remain 1920×1080 for encode and decode

cards.title: Display Size
cards.body: Client --display-width/--display-height: final 800×480 output

cards.title: Start Server
cards.note: Run in the first S100 terminal; -1 enables Camera auto-detection

cards.title: Local Stream URL
cards.note: Use loopback for the first lesson validation

cards.title: Camera Log
cards.note: Confirm resolution, frame rate, and encoder setup

cards.title: Publish Metrics
cards.note: A rising no-client count is normal before Client connects

slides.title: Start Decode and HDMI Output
slides.lead: Keep Server running and take control of HDMI resources from the second terminal

steps.body: Confirm HDMI is connected and the mode list includes 800x480
Let the 30-second test finish, then stop Server

slides.title: Success Must Be Visible
slides.lead: PASS confirms initialization and submissions; final acceptance still requires a visible HDMI image
items: Server encoded and published counters grow at about 30 per second
push-fail=0 and H.264 SPS, PPS, and IDR are nonzero
Client reports linked H264 RTP pad
received and submitted grow at about 30 buffers per second
DRM/GBM initializes and the log reports Display 800x480 channel=11
Live video stays visible with correct aspect, orientation, and color

cards.title: Sensor Probe Warnings
cards.body: Ignore other Chip ID warnings once imx219 is found and initializes

cards.title: Camera Will Not Open
cards.body: Power off; check ribbon orientation, sensor support, and VIO ownership

cards.title: VPU Init Fails
cards.body: Check device nodes, kernel modules, dmesg, and BSP version

cards.title: Connection Refused
cards.body: Confirm Server listens on 8554 and the URL includes /live

cards.title: PASS but Black Screen
cards.body: Stop the desktop and explicitly set channel 11 and 800×480

cards.title: Early EOS
cards.body: Keep Server running until Client exits naturally

slides.data_title: Turn the Loop into a Skill
slides.title: Turn the Loop into a Skill
slides.lead: Camera produces NV12, the BSP owns hardware codec work, GStreamer owns RTSP/RTP, and VPS plus Display produce the final image

cards.title: Compare Bitrate and Quality
cards.body: Change 8000 kbit/s to 4000 and record bitrate and screen quality

cards.title: Change Codec or Transport
cards.body: Switch both endpoints to H.265, or compare RTSP/TCP with UDP

cards.title: Make PASS Stronger
cards.body: Count decoded output and Display submissions to cover real progress
